replies.author: cxfoulke
replies.body:
Making games that rely on multiplayer is scary in general.  As a small indie team... you can sell less copies still make a living and be happy.  For multiplayer you need to start out with explosive numbers or people wont be able to find matches. You can't rely on launch into a gradual decay. For multiplayer moba you need at least 1000+ concurrents at most times in the day. That is an insanely high bar for indie titles.

Id tell basically anyone who is making a game in 2026 avoid multiplayer only like the plague. Normal indie games die on launch 99% of the time. Multiplayer indie games die on launch 99.99% of the time. 

Also Moba's inheriently have a learning curve and skill gaps. So you really want a larger playerbase. So you can protect the new players from vets. 

TLDR; I can think of maybe < 10 multiplayer indie games that sustain themselves. Most of those have some form of you dont need to play multiplayer unlike a moba. 

You basically have to be insane to try.
